This is similar to how we traditionally do it in Croatia ("buzara"). 
Instead of leeks we use garlic, and spices are to personal liking, but more-or-less, the process is the same, and add parsley at the end. 
Oh, and no garum, but really, you get enough umami out of mussels themselves and deglazed wine. 

Some people add breadcrumbs (processed ones) at the end to thicken the sauce.
All sorts of sea food are prepared in the same fashion, with minimal differences.

Author: @batbratsdesigns
Content: I usually steam my muscles in water butter and garlic cloves until the muscles open up. My mom was a crab chucher in Seattle Washington and she taught me how to steam all sorts of shellfish and fish. They still use similar recipes from the mid century. Some people add whole veggies and chopped onions with chives and make a butter sauce by draining some of the leftover liquid and adding corn starch to a sauce pan. You get all of the seafood flavors in the garlic sauce and it goes well with anything. I have made my own seafood garlic butter and added it to my homemade vegetable soup. It's like a seafood stock.
